events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Kassel, Germany; German-born chemist and industrialist.

evidence.quote: Ludwig Mond ( 7 March 1839 – 11 December 1909 ) was a German-born chemist
Ludwig Mond was born into a Jewish family in Kassel , Germany

events.text: Moved to England to work at John Hutchinson & Co factory in Widnes.

evidence.quote: before coming to England to work at the factory of John Hutchinson & Co in Widnes in 1862

events.text: Began working for P. Smits & de Wolf firm in Utrecht.

evidence.quote: He worked in Utrecht for the firm of P .
Smits & de Wolf from 1864 to 1867 and then returned to Widnes

events.text: Married his cousin Frida Löwenthal in Cologne.

evidence.quote: In October 1866 Mond married his cousin Frida Löwenthal

events.text: Left Smits & de Wolf in Utrecht and returned to Widnes.

evidence.quote: Smits & de Wolf from 1864 to 1867 and then returned to Widnes

events.label: contact
events.text: Got in touch with Belgian industrialist Ernest Solvay about the ammonia-soda process.

evidence.quote: In 1872 Mond got in touch with the Belgian industrialist Ernest Solvay

events.text: Went into partnership with John Brunner to commercialise the Solvay process.

evidence.quote: The following year he went into partnership with the industrialist John Brunner

events.label: founding
events.text: Established Brunner Mond & Company, building a factory at Winnington, Northwich.

evidence.quote: They established the business of Brunner Mond & Company , building a factory at Winnington , Northwich

events.text: Turned the Solvay soda ash process into a commercially sound process.

evidence.quote: by 1880 he had turned it into a commercially sound process

events.text: Family moved from Winnington to London.
Elected president of the Society of Chemical Industry.

evidence.quote: of which he was elected president in 1888

events.text: Began spending most winters in Rome at his Palazzo Zuccari home.

evidence.quote: From the early 1890s on, he spent most of his winters in Rome

events.label: honour
events.text: Elected Fellow of the Royal Society.

evidence.quote: He was elected to the Royal Society in 1891

events.text: Rome home Palazzo Zuccari bought in the name of his wife's friend Henriette Hertz.

evidence.quote: This home , the Palazzo Zuccari , was first leased and then ( 1904 ) bought in the name of his wifes

events.label: death
events.text: Died at his London home, The Poplars, Avenue Road.

evidence.quote: Ludwig Mond ( 7 March 1839 – 11 December 1909 ) was a German-born chemist
He died in his London home , The Poplars , Avenue Road , near Regents Park

undated_mentions: Studied chemistry at Marburg (under Kolbe) and Heidelberg (under Bunsen), never gained a degree
Worked in factories in Germany and the Netherlands
Formed partnership with John Hutchinson in Widnes and developed a sulphur recovery method
Discovered nickel carbonyl, basis of the Mond process
Helped expand Lancashire Chemical Society into the Society of Chemical Industry (with Henry Roscoe)
Elected member of the German Chemical Society and the Società Reale of Naples
Received honorary doctorates from Padua, Heidelberg, Manchester and Oxford
Awarded grand cordon of the Order of the Crown of Italy
Benefactor to scientific organisations (Royal Society, Accademia dei Lincei, Royal Institution)
Became largest producer of soda ash in the world (within 20 years of the partnership)
Left bequests in his will to Kassel and Jewish charities, and old master paintings to the National Gallery London
Buried with Jewish rites at St Pancras cemetery
